passages.context: Chrysostom's argument that the disposition of the burial cloths tells against theft of the body, read on printed pages 320 and 321 rendered from the hashed facsimile. The reading included the preceding paragraph on the placing of the tomb, footnote 11 on page 320 which quotes John 20:3-7, and the opening of section 5 on page 321, so that the passage boundary is explicit.
passages.notes: The homily's printed scriptural heading is John 19:16-18; the exposition of the tomb scene stands in section 4. The sentence beginning Nor was it for these reasons only, on the placing of the tomb so that the story about the stealing might be proved false, stands earlier in the same section and is not transcribed here.

passages.context: The opening of the homily on John 20:10-11, read on printed page 323 rendered from the hashed facsimile, for Chrysostom's statement that the two disciples had seen the linen clothes and believed. The homily's own heading, HOMILY LXXXVI, John xx. 10, 11, was read with it.
passages.notes: Later in the same section Chrysostom writes that the woman's mind was not sufficiently elevated to accept the Resurrection from the proof of the napkins; that clause was read on the same page and is not transcribed here.

work.author: Philip Schaff
work.description: The fourteenth volume of the first series of the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers translation anthology, containing the English of Chrysostom's eighty-eight homilies on the Gospel of John, revised by Frederic Gardiner from the Oxford Library of Fathers version of Charles Marriott, together with the homilies on Hebrews. Its container identity remains distinct from Chrysostom's own works and from the translated editions printed within it. Homily LXXXV takes John 19:16-18 as its printed lemma and runs through John 20:10; Homily LXXXVI takes John 20:10-11.
work.title: A Select Library of the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers of the Christian Church, First Series, Volume XIV
